title: Greetings and introductions
description: Practise simple greetings and introducing yourself.
content: A friendly greeting can help you feel more confident when meeting people in Aotearoa New Zealand. You can say hello, share your name, and ask how someone is.

phrases.text: Kia ora. My name is Amina.
phrases.meaning: Hello. My name is Amina.

phrases.text: Nice to meet you.
phrases.meaning: A polite phrase when meeting someone.

phrases.text: Could you please say that again?
phrases.meaning: Ask someone to repeat something.

tip: Kia ora is a common Māori greeting used by many people in New Zealand.

title: Te reo Māori: useful words
description: Learn a few everyday Māori words and greetings.
content: Te reo Māori is an official language of Aotearoa New Zealand. Start by listening carefully and practising a few words respectfully. Māori pronunciation uses clear vowel sounds.

phrases.text: Kia ora.
phrases.meaning: Hello, thank you, or a warm expression of regard, depending on context.

phrases.text: Aotearoa.
phrases.meaning: The Māori name commonly used for New Zealand.

phrases.text: Haere mai.
phrases.meaning: Welcome; come here.

tip: Try saying each phrase slowly. Māori vowels are generally pronounced clearly: a, e, i, o, u.

title: Looking for accommodation
description: Practise questions to ask when viewing a room or home.
content: When searching for a place to live, clarify the rent, bond, bills, move-in date, and what is included. Read agreements carefully and ask questions if anything is unclear.

phrases.text: How much is the rent each week?
phrases.meaning: Ask about the weekly rent.

phrases.text: Are any bills included?
phrases.meaning: Ask whether utilities are part of the rent.

phrases.text: When is the room available?
phrases.meaning: Ask about the move-in date.

tip: Housing rules and rental arrangements can vary. Check current information from official New Zealand sources before signing an agreement.

title: Ordering at a café
description: Practise a simple café order and asking about options.
content: Cafés are a useful place to practise everyday English. Speak at your own pace, and ask the staff to repeat or explain something if needed.

phrases.text: Could I please have a flat white?
phrases.meaning: A polite way to order a coffee.

phrases.text: What non-dairy milk do you have?
phrases.meaning: Ask about alternatives to dairy milk.

phrases.text: Could I have the receipt, please?
phrases.meaning: Ask for proof of payment.

tip: You can replace “flat white” with the food or drink you would like.

title: Community, respect, and local customs
description: Explore respectful ways to take part in community life.
content: Aotearoa New Zealand is home to people from many cultures. Customs differ between communities and situations. Listening, asking politely, and showing respect are good ways to learn.

phrases.text: Could you tell me more about that?
phrases.meaning: Show interest and invite someone to explain.

phrases.text: Please let me know if I should do this differently.
phrases.meaning: Invite guidance in a considerate way.

phrases.text: Thank you for welcoming me.
phrases.meaning: Express appreciation for being included.

tip: When learning about Māori culture, use trusted Māori-led resources and follow local guidance.

title: Getting around and asking for help
description: Practise asking for directions and everyday assistance.
content: It is normal to ask for directions when you are somewhere new. Mention your destination and listen for landmarks, street names, or transport details.

phrases.text: Excuse me, how do I get to the bus station?
phrases.meaning: Ask someone for directions.

phrases.text: Which bus should I take?
phrases.meaning: Ask about a bus route.

phrases.text: Could you show me on the map?
phrases.meaning: Ask someone to point out a location.

tip: Transport services and routes differ between places. Check your local transport provider for current details.

title: A brief introduction to Aotearoa history
description: Begin learning about Māori history and the formation of modern New Zealand.
content: Aotearoa New Zealand has a long Māori history. The Treaty of Waitangi (Te Tiriti o Waitangi) was signed in 1840 by representatives of the British Crown and many Māori rangatira. Its history, meanings, and effects are significant and have been understood differently by different people.

phrases.text: I am learning about the history of Aotearoa.
phrases.meaning: Share that you are studying New Zealand history.

phrases.text: Where can I learn more about Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
phrases.meaning: Ask for a learning resource about the Treaty.

phrases.text: Thank you for sharing your perspective.
phrases.meaning: A respectful response to someone sharing their view.

tip: This is only a brief introduction, not a full account. Seek Māori perspectives and reputable historical resources for deeper learning.
